To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Choquet integral may be tolerant or intolerant depending on the criteria it aggregates, and that this tolerance is characterized by a set of indices measuring the tolerance of each of these criteria, and by a global tolerance index measuring the tolerance of the aggregation operator.

the Choquet integral can be conjunctive or (more often) disjunctive, that a criterion can be a veto or a pusher (or both) and that a veto (pusher) is a conjunctive criterion (a disjunctive criterion) that bounds the aggregation from above (from below).

the tolerance of the Choquet integral can be measured by a global index, and that each criterion has an associated tolerance degree that can be measured by an index that is related to the veto and favor degrees.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the tolerance of the Choquet integral as an aggregation operator and with the tolerance of criteria in the aggregation.
the analysis of the tolerance of the criteria as well as the tolerance of the aggregation procedure, in the context of aggregation by the Chochet integral.
the tolerant and intolerant behavior of the Choquet integral, and the criteria that it aggregates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a Choquet integral is tolerant (conjunctive) when all its criteria are tolerant (conjunctively interacting) and intolerant (disjunctive) when at least one of them is intolerant (disjunctorily interacting).
the Choquet integral behaves in a conjunctive way when it is tolerant and in a disjunctive way when not.

the Choquet integral can be considered as tolerant (resp. intolerant) if it is conjunctive (resp. disjunctive), and that the criteria can be considered as intolerant (resp. tolerant) if they behave like vetos (resp. favors).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a way to characterize and quantify the tolerance of the Choquet integral, which in turns enables the decision maker to better understand the nature and the extent to which criteria interact.
, given a Choquet integral, the more tolerant the integral is, the more tolerant are its criteria.
we provide the means to analyze the tolerant character of the interaction of criteria in the aggregation by Choquet integral.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tolerance degrees of the Choquet integral are not necessarily related to the tolerance of the criteria.
the Choquet integral can be viewed as an aggregation operator that is either conjunctive or, in the presence of a few decisive (veto or favor) criteria, disjunctive.
these tolerance degrees can be computed in a very easy manner.
